newsitem.title: ITALY: Fiat 1996 profits up, but Q1 disappoints.
newsitem.headline: Fiat 1996 profits up, but Q1 disappoints.

text.p: Italy's industrial giant Fiat on Thursday reported a 10.4 percent rise in 1996 net profits boosted by one-off income gains, but the first quarter 1997 saw profits slip as the group struggled for recovery.

Fiat showed a 1996 net profit of 2.371 trillion lire ($1.4 billion) against 1995's 2.147 trillion, but this masked an underlying decline since 1996 was boosted by on-offs amounting to 1.4 trillion lire from the flotation of a 31 percent stake in New Holland and the sale of its fund management arm Prime.

Analysts said underlying net profits for 1996 were below one trillion lire and the first quarter saw operating profits and profit margins decline as Italy's car buying incentive scheme only began to make an impact on Fiat's finances in March.

Fiat said in a statement that in the first quarter of 1997 its pretax profit rose to 495 billion lire from 464 billion in the first quarter of 1996, but 1997 first quarter operating profits slipped to 450 billion lire from 504 billion lire.

First quarter industrial margins slipped to 2.6 percent which compared to 2.9 percent for the whole of 1996 and 4.9 percent in 1995. However, Fiat said margins were on an improving trend in the first quarter, particularly clear in March.

"The first quarter figures were clearly a little disappointing," said analyst Bob Barber at HSBC James Capel. He pointed out that export sales were hit by the strong lira and although the domestic Italian car market had improved it came at the cost to Fiat of the new car incentive scheme.

Italy introduced a new car buying incentive scheme in January this year to run to end-September offering owners of cars older than 10 years a discount to trade them in and buy a new one. The scheme is financed equally by the government and the Italian car industry.

"Clearly the benefits of the incentive scheme were not in the first quarter, but I am sticking to my operating margin forecast of 3.2 percent for the year on sales of 86.7 trillion lire," said analyst Nick Potter at Credito Italiano.

Group first quarter 1997 sales rose 4.4 percent to 20.844 trillion lire, while automotive unit Fiat Auto said it sold some 628,000 vehicles showing a rise of 3.7 percent from first quarter 1996 levels.

Despite a strong rise in Italian car sales in the first months of 1997 due to the incentive scheme many analysts remained sceptical of these artifical aids to the market, especially after the French ended their incentive scheme and their industry sees sales dipping 11.4 percent in 1997.

One analyst said when incentive schemes are stopped, volumes dip, producers need to cut prices to try to shift stocks while consumers are not as responsive to price cuts after seeing the benefits of the incentive scheme.

Fiat announced an unchanged 1996 ordinary dividend of 100 lire/share after it had doubled it from 1995 and also left unchanged its 130 lire saving share dividend. The group also added that it was to make a one-for-10 bonus share issue to shareholders on the company register at the start of 1997.
Fiat group consolidated debt slipped to 2.211 trillion lire at end-1996 from 2.597 trillion lire at end-1995.

Market dealers said that Fiat shares appeared to sense disappointing results, which came after the Milan market closed, and the shares ended off 2.83 percent at 5,429 lire in one of the biggest fall in an overall lower stock market. ($1=1,706 lire)
